category: Self-hosted password and secrets management for organisations: a team password manager for people (personal vault, sharing, browser autofill, emergency access) combined with a write-without-read secret store, leases and a private certificate authority for applications, running inside the organisation's own Nextcloud with zero-knowledge encryption. A buyer, typically a Dutch public body wanting credentials kept on its own infrastructure, compares it with the SaaS team password managers (Bitwarden, 1Password, Keeper), the self-hosted open-source team manager Passbolt, the machine-secrets engine HashiCorp Vault for the application side, and the community Nextcloud Passwords app as the in-platform alternative. Decided from the code on 2026-09-26 (appinfo/info.xml, lib/Controller, 45 specs under openspec/specs); no prior competitor research exists for this product under any of its names.

capabilities.name: The certificate authority renews its own certificates before they expire.

built.evidence: Intermediate: lib/BackgroundJob/RenewIntermediateCertificate.php:68 (daily, appinfo/info.xml:111) -> CertificateAuthorityService.php:242 renewIntermediate -> resignAllActiveSuites. Root: CertificateAuthorityService.php:288 renewRoot only reachable through POST /api/v1/ca/renew-root (lib/Controller/CACertificateController.php:140), which no UI calls (routes-unmatched NO-REF); lib/BackgroundJob/CheckRootCertificateExpiry.php:68 only logs
built.reachedOn: machine: daily background job (intermediate only)
built.note: The intermediate is renewed automatically, but because of an inverted date diff it is renewed every day rather than 30 days before expiry. The root is never renewed automatically and its expiry warning never fires.

defects.what: daysUntilExpiry is computed as $expiresAt->diff(now), which is negative while the certificate is still valid (php -r confirms -299 for +300 days), so the 'more than 30 days left' early return never fires and the job renews the intermediate and re-signs every active suite on every daily run.
Same inverted diff: daysUntilExpiry is negative for a valid root, so the 90/30/7 day warnings never match. The job only ever logs anyway; it sends no notification and does not renew.

capabilities.name: Use the extension as a passkey provider on websites.

built.evidence: browser-extension/src/content/content-script.js:192 injectShim -> browser-extension/src/content/inpage-shim.js overrides navigator.credentials -> content-script.js:204 relay -> service-worker.js:230 webauthn-create/get -> browser-extension/src/passkey/orchestrator.js:74 handleCreate (consent window, createSecret with passkey typeId) / handleGet (match by rpId, getAssertion browser-extension/src/passkey/webauthn.js:197, counter write-back); native path browser-extension/src/passkey/registration.js:23

built.note: Passkey create and sign run in the extension through the page shim with per-site consent. The Chrome native proxy path never activates because its optional permission is never requested, and the relay trusts an origin the page itself supplies.

defects.what: The extension has no release or store pipeline (only cli-release.yml exists under .github/workflows), so a user can only get it by building from source and loading it unpacked.

The relay forwards data.origin from the page's own postMessage instead of location.origin, and no code checks the rpId against the origin, so a malicious page can ask for an assertion for another site's rpId with a forged origin in clientDataJSON; only the consent window naming that rpId stands in the way.
webAuthenticationProxy is an optional permission and nothing calls chrome.permissions.request, so registration.js:26 always finds no proxy and the native Chrome/Edge provider path is dead.
